definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Conducting impulses or fluids toward a central point. Afferent nerve fibers carry sensory signals toward the central nervous system; afferent vessels carry blood toward an organ.
description_en: Conducting impulses or fluids toward a central point. Afferent nerve fibers carry sensory signals toward the central nervous system; afferent vessels carry blood toward an organ.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The standard reference posture used in anatomy: body erect, face forward, feet together, arms at the sides with palms facing anteriorly. All anatomical terms of direction are defined relative to this position.
description_en: The standard reference posture used in anatomy: body erect, face forward, feet together, arms at the sides with palms facing anteriorly. All anatomical terms of direction are defined relative to this position.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated toward the front of the body. In anatomical position, the anterior surface faces forward. Synonymous with ventral in standard anatomical position.
description_en: Situated toward the front of the body. In anatomical position, the anterior surface faces forward. Synonymous with ventral in standard anatomical position.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: On the opposite side of the body. Most descending motor and ascending pain pathways decussate (cross), so lesions produce contralateral deficits.
description_en: On the opposite side of the body. Most descending motor and ascending pain pathways decussate (cross), so lesions produce contralateral deficits.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A vertical plane that divides the body into anterior and posterior portions, also called the frontal plane. It passes perpendicular to the sagittal plane.
description_en: A vertical plane that divides the body into anterior and posterior portions, also called the frontal plane. It passes perpendicular to the sagittal plane.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Located further from the body surface, beneath more superficial structures. Deep muscles lie beneath superficial muscles and closer to bone.
description_en: Located further from the body surface, beneath more superficial structures. Deep muscles lie beneath superficial muscles and closer to bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated further from the point of origin or attachment, typically the trunk. Used primarily for limb structures where distal means further from the body's midline.
description_en: Situated further from the point of origin or attachment, typically the trunk. Used primarily for limb structures where distal means further from the body's midline.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Pertaining to the back surface of the body; synonymous with posterior in humans. Dorsal also describes the top surface of the foot (dorsum pedis) and hand (dorsum manus).
description_en: Pertaining to the back surface of the body; synonymous with posterior in humans. Dorsal also describes the top surface of the foot (dorsum pedis) and hand (dorsum manus).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Conducting impulses or fluids away from a central point. Efferent nerve fibers carry motor signals away from the CNS to muscles and glands; efferent vessels carry blood away from an organ.
description_en: Conducting impulses or fluids away from a central point. Efferent nerve fibers carry motor signals away from the CNS to muscles and glands; efferent vessels carry blood away from an organ.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated below or toward the foot end of the body (also called caudal). The kidneys are inferior to the diaphragm.
description_en: Situated below or toward the foot end of the body (also called caudal). The kidneys are inferior to the diaphragm.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: On the same side of the body. Ipsilateral motor and sensory pathways travel on the same side without crossing; the term is clinically important in neurological localization.
description_en: On the same side of the body. Ipsilateral motor and sensory pathways travel on the same side without crossing; the term is clinically important in neurological localization.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated further from the median plane (midline) of the body. The fibula is lateral to the tibia in the leg.
description_en: Situated further from the median plane (midline) of the body. The fibula is lateral to the tibia in the leg.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated closer to the median plane (midline) of the body. The ulna is medial to the radius in the forearm.
description_en: Situated closer to the median plane (midline) of the body. The ulna is medial to the radius in the forearm.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated toward the back of the body. In anatomical position, the posterior surface faces backward. Synonymous with dorsal in standard anatomical position.
description_en: Situated toward the back of the body. In anatomical position, the posterior surface faces backward. Synonymous with dorsal in standard anatomical position.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated closer to the point of origin or attachment, typically the trunk. Used primarily for limb structures where proximal means closer to the body's midline.
description_en: Situated closer to the point of origin or attachment, typically the trunk. Used primarily for limb structures where proximal means closer to the body's midline.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A vertical plane that divides the body into left and right portions. The midsagittal (median) plane passes through the midline; parasagittal planes are parallel but offset from the midline.
description_en: A vertical plane that divides the body into left and right portions. The midsagittal (median) plane passes through the midline; parasagittal planes are parallel but offset from the midline.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Located closer to the body surface. Superficial structures are closer to the skin than deep structures of the same region.
description_en: Located closer to the body surface. Superficial structures are closer to the skin than deep structures of the same region.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Situated above or toward the head end of the body (also called cranial). The heart is superior to the diaphragm.
description_en: Situated above or toward the head end of the body (also called cranial). The heart is superior to the diaphragm.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A horizontal plane that divides the body into superior and inferior portions, also called the axial or cross-sectional plane. CT and MRI images are commonly displayed in this orientation.
description_en: A horizontal plane that divides the body into superior and inferior portions, also called the axial or cross-sectional plane. CT and MRI images are commonly displayed in this orientation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Pertaining to the belly or front surface of the body; synonymous with anterior in humans. In four-legged animals, ventral refers to the underside of the body.
description_en: Pertaining to the belly or front surface of the body; synonymous with anterior in humans. In four-legged animals, ventral refers to the underside of the body.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The tough outer fibrocartilaginous ring of an intervertebral disc that surrounds and contains the gelatinous nucleus pulposus. Tears in the annulus fibrosus allow disc herniation.
description_en: The tough outer fibrocartilaginous ring of an intervertebral disc that surrounds and contains the gelatinous nucleus pulposus. Tears in the annulus fibrosus allow disc herniation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A joint or point of contact between two or more bones. Articulations are classified as fibrous (immovable), cartilaginous (slightly movable), or synovial (freely movable).
description_en: A joint or point of contact between two or more bones. Articulations are classified as fibrous (immovable), cartilaginous (slightly movable), or synovial (freely movable).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A fluid-filled sac lined with synovial membrane that reduces friction between tendons, muscles, and bony prominences. Inflammation of a bursa (bursitis) is a common cause of joint pain.
description_en: A fluid-filled sac lined with synovial membrane that reduces friction between tendons, muscles, and bony prominences. Inflammation of a bursa (bursitis) is a common cause of joint pain.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The site where a tendon, ligament, or joint capsule attaches to bone. Enthesopathy (inflammation at entheses) is a hallmark of seronegative spondyloarthropathies such as ankylosing spondylitis.
description_en: The site where a tendon, ligament, or joint capsule attaches to bone. Enthesopathy (inflammation at entheses) is a hallmark of seronegative spondyloarthropathies such as ankylosing spondylitis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A sheet or band of fibrous connective tissue that envelops, separates, and supports muscles and organs. Deep fascia compartmentalizes muscle groups; superficial fascia lies beneath the skin.
description_en: A sheet or band of fibrous connective tissue that envelops, separates, and supports muscles and organs. Deep fascia compartmentalizes muscle groups; superficial fascia lies beneath the skin.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The distal, usually more movable attachment point of a skeletal muscle. During contraction, the insertion is drawn toward the origin to produce movement.
description_en: The distal, usually more movable attachment point of a skeletal muscle. During contraction, the insertion is drawn toward the origin to produce movement.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A sheet of deep fascia extending inward from the outer investing fascia to attach to bone, separating adjacent muscle compartments. Injury or swelling within a compartment can raise pressure and cause compartment syndrome.
description_en: A sheet of deep fascia extending inward from the outer investing fascia to attach to bone, separating adjacent muscle compartments. Injury or swelling within a compartment can raise pressure and cause compartment syndrome.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A fibrocartilaginous cushion between adjacent vertebral bodies consisting of an outer annulus fibrosus and an inner nucleus pulposus. Discs account for roughly 25% of total spine height and allow spinal flexibility.
description_en: A fibrocartilaginous cushion between adjacent vertebral bodies consisting of an outer annulus fibrosus and an inner nucleus pulposus. Discs account for roughly 25% of total spine height and allow spinal flexibility.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outermost layer of deep fascia that encircles an entire limb or body region, encasing all structures within it. In the lower limb, the investing fascia is called the fascia lata.
description_en: The outermost layer of deep fascia that encircles an entire limb or body region, encasing all structures within it. In the lower limb, the investing fascia is called the fascia lata.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A ring of fibrocartilage attached to the rim of certain joint sockets (particularly the hip and shoulder glenoid) that deepens the articular cavity and improves joint stability. Labral tears are a common sports injury.
description_en: A ring of fibrocartilage attached to the rim of certain joint sockets (particularly the hip and shoulder glenoid) that deepens the articular cavity and improves joint stability. Labral tears are a common sports injury.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects bone to bone, providing stability to joints. Ligaments limit excessive movement and prevent dislocation.
description_en: A band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects bone to bone, providing stability to joints. Ligaments limit excessive movement and prevent dislocation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A crescent-shaped fibrocartilage pad found in certain joints, most notably the knee. Menisci improve joint congruence, distribute load across the articular surface, and aid in shock absorption.
description_en: A crescent-shaped fibrocartilage pad found in certain joints, most notably the knee. Menisci improve joint congruence, distribute load across the articular surface, and aid in shock absorption.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The interface where muscle fibers meet tendon, representing the transition zone between contractile and non-contractile tissue. This region is a common site of muscle strains during eccentric loading.
description_en: The interface where muscle fibers meet tendon, representing the transition zone between contractile and non-contractile tissue. This region is a common site of muscle strains during eccentric loading.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The gelatinous, water-rich core of an intervertebral disc that acts as a shock absorber and distributes compressive forces. It is a remnant of the embryonic notochord.
description_en: The gelatinous, water-rich core of an intervertebral disc that acts as a shock absorber and distributes compressive forces. It is a remnant of the embryonic notochord.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The proximal, usually less movable attachment point of a skeletal muscle. During contraction, the origin remains relatively fixed while the insertion moves toward it.
description_en: The proximal, usually less movable attachment point of a skeletal muscle. During contraction, the origin remains relatively fixed while the insertion moves toward it.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A seam or ridge of tissue formed where two symmetrical halves meet, often serving as a tendinous intersection or midline union. The pterygomandibular raphe is a clinically important landmark in dental anesthesia.
description_en: A seam or ridge of tissue formed where two symmetrical halves meet, often serving as a tendinous intersection or midline union. The pterygomandibular raphe is a clinically important landmark in dental anesthesia.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A small bone embedded within a tendon, typically near a joint, that protects the tendon and improves its mechanical advantage. The patella is the largest sesamoid bone in the human body.
description_en: A small bone embedded within a tendon, typically near a joint, that protects the tendon and improves its mechanical advantage. The patella is the largest sesamoid bone in the human body.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A viscous, egg-white-like fluid secreted by the synovial membrane that lubricates synovial joints and provides nutrients to avascular articular cartilage. Its viscosity is due to hyaluronic acid.
description_en: A viscous, egg-white-like fluid secreted by the synovial membrane that lubricates synovial joints and provides nutrients to avascular articular cartilage. Its viscosity is due to hyaluronic acid.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The inner lining of a joint capsule that secretes synovial fluid to lubricate and nourish articular cartilage. Inflammation of the synovial membrane (synovitis) is characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.
description_en: The inner lining of a joint capsule that secretes synovial fluid to lubricate and nourish articular cartilage. Inflammation of the synovial membrane (synovitis) is characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A fibrous band of connective tissue that attaches a muscle to a bone. Tendons transmit the force of muscle contraction to produce movement at joints.
description_en: A fibrous band of connective tissue that attaches a muscle to a bone. Tendons transmit the force of muscle contraction to produce movement at joints.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A connection between two blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, or other tubular structures. Arterial anastomoses provide collateral circulation to maintain blood supply if one vessel is occluded.
description_en: A connection between two blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, or other tubular structures. Arterial anastomoses provide collateral circulation to maintain blood supply if one vessel is occluded.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cluster of specialized conduction cells at the base of the right atrium near the interventricular septum that delays electrical transmission between the atria and ventricles, allowing atrial contraction to complete before ventricular contraction begins.
description_en: A cluster of specialized conduction cells at the base of the right atrium near the interventricular septum that delays electrical transmission between the atria and ventricles, allowing atrial contraction to complete before ventricular contraction begins.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: One of the two superior receiving chambers of the heart. The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation via the vena cavae; the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins.
description_en: One of the two superior receiving chambers of the heart. The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation via the vena cavae; the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A collection of heart muscle cells (specialized cardiac fibers) that transmit electrical impulses from the atrioventricular node to the right and left bundle branches and then to the Purkinje fibers. Also called the atrioventricular bundle.
description_en: A collection of heart muscle cells (specialized cardiac fibers) that transmit electrical impulses from the atrioventricular node to the right and left bundle branches and then to the Purkinje fibers. Also called the atrioventricular bundle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The phase of the cardiac cycle when the heart chambers relax and fill with blood. Ventricular diastole allows the ventricles to receive blood from the atria.
description_en: The phase of the cardiac cycle when the heart chambers relax and fill with blood. Ventricular diastole allows the ventricles to receive blood from the atria.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The thin inner lining of the heart chambers and cardiac valves, continuous with the endothelium of blood vessels. Endocarditis is a serious infection of this layer, particularly affecting valves.
description_en: The thin inner lining of the heart chambers and cardiac valves, continuous with the endothelium of blood vessels. Endocarditis is a serious infection of this layer, particularly affecting valves.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The single layer of squamous epithelial cells lining the interior surface of blood vessels and lymphatic vessels. The endothelium regulates vascular tone, coagulation, and inflammation.
description_en: The single layer of squamous epithelial cells lining the interior surface of blood vessels and lymphatic vessels. The endothelium regulates vascular tone, coagulation, and inflammation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The interior space of a tubular structure, such as a blood vessel or intestine. The diameter of the vascular lumen determines blood flow and resistance.
description_en: The interior space of a tubular structure, such as a blood vessel or intestine. The diameter of the vascular lumen determines blood flow and resistance.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The muscular middle layer of the heart wall, composed of specialized cardiac muscle cells (cardiomyocytes). It constitutes the bulk of the heart and is responsible for the pumping action.
description_en: The muscular middle layer of the heart wall, composed of specialized cardiac muscle cells (cardiomyocytes). It constitutes the bulk of the heart and is responsible for the pumping action.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The passage of blood through the vascular bed of a tissue or organ. Adequate perfusion is essential for oxygen and nutrient delivery and waste removal.
description_en: The passage of blood through the vascular bed of a tissue or organ. Adequate perfusion is essential for oxygen and nutrient delivery and waste removal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The double-layered fibroserous sac enclosing the heart and the roots of the great vessels. The fibrous pericardium limits over-distension; the serous pericardium secretes pericardial fluid to reduce friction.
description_en: The double-layered fibroserous sac enclosing the heart and the roots of the great vessels. The fibrous pericardium limits over-distension; the serous pericardium secretes pericardial fluid to reduce friction.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Specialized cardiac muscle fibers in the subendocardial layer that rapidly conduct electrical impulses from the bundle branches to the ventricular myocardium, ensuring synchronous ventricular contraction.
description_en: Specialized cardiac muscle fibers in the subendocardial layer that rapidly conduct electrical impulses from the bundle branches to the ventricular myocardium, ensuring synchronous ventricular contraction.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The muscular wall dividing the heart into left and right halves. The interventricular septum separates the two ventricles; the interatrial septum separates the two atria. Septal defects are common congenital heart anomalies.
description_en: The muscular wall dividing the heart into left and right halves. The interventricular septum separates the two ventricles; the interatrial septum separates the two atria. Septal defects are common congenital heart anomalies.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cluster of pacemaker cells in the right atrial wall near the opening of the superior vena cava that spontaneously generates electrical impulses, setting the intrinsic heart rate. Also called the SA node or cardiac pacemaker.
description_en: A cluster of pacemaker cells in the right atrial wall near the opening of the superior vena cava that spontaneously generates electrical impulses, setting the intrinsic heart rate. Also called the SA node or cardiac pacemaker.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The phase of the cardiac cycle when the heart chambers contract and pump blood. Ventricular systole ejects blood into the aorta and pulmonary artery.
description_en: The phase of the cardiac cycle when the heart chambers contract and pump blood. Ventricular systole ejects blood into the aorta and pulmonary artery.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outermost layer of a blood vessel wall, composed of fibrous connective tissue that anchors the vessel to surrounding structures. It contains the vasa vasorum (tiny vessels supplying the vessel wall) and autonomic nerve fibers.
description_en: The outermost layer of a blood vessel wall, composed of fibrous connective tissue that anchors the vessel to surrounding structures. It contains the vasa vasorum (tiny vessels supplying the vessel wall) and autonomic nerve fibers.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The innermost layer of a blood vessel wall, consisting of endothelium resting on a thin basement membrane and a subendothelial connective tissue layer. Atherosclerotic plaques develop within the tunica intima.
description_en: The innermost layer of a blood vessel wall, consisting of endothelium resting on a thin basement membrane and a subendothelial connective tissue layer. Atherosclerotic plaques develop within the tunica intima.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The middle layer of a blood vessel wall, composed of smooth muscle and elastic tissue. It is the thickest layer in arteries and controls vessel diameter and hence blood pressure.
description_en: The middle layer of a blood vessel wall, composed of smooth muscle and elastic tissue. It is the thickest layer in arteries and controls vessel diameter and hence blood pressure.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A structure that ensures unidirectional blood flow through the heart. The four cardiac valves are the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic valves; they open and close passively in response to pressure gradients.
description_en: A structure that ensures unidirectional blood flow through the heart. The four cardiac valves are the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic valves; they open and close passively in response to pressure gradients.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: One of the two inferior pumping chambers of the heart. The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs; the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.
description_en: One of the two inferior pumping chambers of the heart. The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs; the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Star-shaped glial cells that are the most abundant cells in the brain. Astrocytes maintain the blood-brain barrier, regulate extracellular ion concentrations, provide metabolic support to neurons, and participate in synaptic modulation.
description_en: Star-shaped glial cells that are the most abundant cells in the brain. Astrocytes maintain the blood-brain barrier, regulate extracellular ion concentrations, provide metabolic support to neurons, and participate in synaptic modulation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The long, slender projection of a neuron that conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body toward other neurons or effector organs. Axons may be myelinated or unmyelinated and can extend over a meter in length.
description_en: The long, slender projection of a neuron that conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body toward other neurons or effector organs. Axons may be myelinated or unmyelinated and can extend over a meter in length.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A selective permeability barrier formed by tight junctions between cerebral endothelial cells, supported by astrocyte foot processes, that tightly regulates the passage of substances from blood into brain tissue. It protects the CNS from pathogens and toxins but also limits drug delivery.
description_en: A selective permeability barrier formed by tight junctions between cerebral endothelial cells, supported by astrocyte foot processes, that tightly regulates the passage of substances from blood into brain tissue. It protects the CNS from pathogens and toxins but also limits drug delivery.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The region connecting the cerebrum and cerebellum to the spinal cord, consisting of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. It contains vital autonomic centers for respiration, cardiovascular regulation, and the nuclei of most cranial nerves.
description_en: The region connecting the cerebrum and cerebellum to the spinal cord, consisting of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. It contains vital autonomic centers for respiration, cardiovascular regulation, and the nuclei of most cranial nerves.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The large hindbrain structure posterior to the brainstem that coordinates voluntary movement, balance, and motor learning. Cerebellar damage produces ataxia (incoordination) and dysmetria (inability to judge distances).
description_en: The large hindbrain structure posterior to the brainstem that coordinates voluntary movement, balance, and motor learning. Cerebellar damage produces ataxia (incoordination) and dysmetria (inability to judge distances).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outer layer of gray matter covering the cerebral hemispheres, organized into six cellular layers (laminae). It is responsible for higher cognitive functions including consciousness, sensory perception, language, and voluntary motor control.
description_en: The outer layer of gray matter covering the cerebral hemispheres, organized into six cellular layers (laminae). It is responsible for higher cognitive functions including consciousness, sensory perception, language, and voluntary motor control.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Branching cytoplasmic extensions of a neuron that receive synaptic inputs from other neurons and conduct electrical signals toward the cell body. Most neurons have multiple dendrites, greatly increasing their surface area for synaptic contact.
description_en: Branching cytoplasmic extensions of a neuron that receive synaptic inputs from other neurons and conduct electrical signals toward the cell body. Most neurons have multiple dendrites, greatly increasing their surface area for synaptic contact.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An area of skin supplied by sensory nerve fibers from a single spinal nerve root. Dermatome maps are used clinically to localize spinal cord and nerve root lesions.
description_en: An area of skin supplied by sensory nerve fibers from a single spinal nerve root. Dermatome maps are used clinically to localize spinal cord and nerve root lesions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cluster of neuron cell bodies located outside the central nervous system. Dorsal root ganglia contain sensory neuron cell bodies; autonomic ganglia contain postganglionic neuron cell bodies.
description_en: A cluster of neuron cell bodies located outside the central nervous system. Dorsal root ganglia contain sensory neuron cell bodies; autonomic ganglia contain postganglionic neuron cell bodies.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Non-neuronal supporting cells of the nervous system that provide structural support, insulation, nutrients, and immune defense. Glia outnumber neurons in the brain and include astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and ependymal cells.
description_en: Non-neuronal supporting cells of the nervous system that provide structural support, insulation, nutrients, and immune defense. Glia outnumber neurons in the brain and include astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and ependymal cells.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A small region at the base of the diencephalon that controls the autonomic nervous system, regulates pituitary hormone secretion, and maintains homeostasis of body temperature, hunger, thirst, and circadian rhythms.
description_en: A small region at the base of the diencephalon that controls the autonomic nervous system, regulates pituitary hormone secretion, and maintains homeostasis of body temperature, hunger, thirst, and circadian rhythms.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The three protective membranes (dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater) surrounding the brain and spinal cord. They contain cerebrospinal fluid and protect the central nervous system.
description_en: The three protective membranes (dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater) surrounding the brain and spinal cord. They contain cerebrospinal fluid and protect the central nervous system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A fatty insulating sheath surrounding many nerve fibers that increases the speed of electrical impulse conduction. Produced by Schwann cells in the PNS and oligodendrocytes in the CNS.
description_en: A fatty insulating sheath surrounding many nerve fibers that increases the speed of electrical impulse conduction. Produced by Schwann cells in the PNS and oligodendrocytes in the CNS.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The fundamental excitable cell of the nervous system, specialized for receiving and transmitting electrical and chemical signals. A neuron consists of a cell body (soma), dendrites, and an axon.
description_en: The fundamental excitable cell of the nervous system, specialized for receiving and transmitting electrical and chemical signals. A neuron consists of a cell body (soma), dendrites, and an axon.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Glial cells of the central nervous system that produce myelin sheaths around axons, enabling rapid saltatory conduction. A single oligodendrocyte can myelinate up to 50 axon segments; their destruction underlies demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis.
description_en: Glial cells of the central nervous system that produce myelin sheaths around axons, enabling rapid saltatory conduction. A single oligodendrocyte can myelinate up to 50 axon segments; their destruction underlies demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A network of intersecting nerves or blood vessels. Major nerve plexuses include the cervical, brachial, lumbar, and sacral plexuses that supply the limbs and body wall.
description_en: A network of intersecting nerves or blood vessels. Major nerve plexuses include the cervical, brachial, lumbar, and sacral plexuses that supply the limbs and body wall.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Glial cells of the peripheral nervous system that form myelin sheaths around axons. Unlike oligodendrocytes, each Schwann cell myelinates only one axon segment; they also facilitate peripheral nerve regeneration after injury.
description_en: Glial cells of the peripheral nervous system that form myelin sheaths around axons. Unlike oligodendrocytes, each Schwann cell myelinates only one axon segment; they also facilitate peripheral nerve regeneration after injury.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The cylindrical bundle of neural tissue extending from the medulla oblongata to the conus medullaris (approximately L1-L2 vertebral level). It contains ascending sensory tracts and descending motor tracts, and mediates spinal reflexes.
description_en: The cylindrical bundle of neural tissue extending from the medulla oblongata to the conus medullaris (approximately L1-L2 vertebral level). It contains ascending sensory tracts and descending motor tracts, and mediates spinal reflexes.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The junction between two neurons or between a neuron and an effector cell. Neurotransmitters released at synapses transmit signals across the synaptic cleft.
description_en: The junction between two neurons or between a neuron and an effector cell. Neurotransmitters released at synapses transmit signals across the synaptic cleft.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A paired gray-matter structure in the diencephalon that serves as the major relay station for sensory and motor signals to and from the cerebral cortex. Nearly all sensory information (except olfaction) is processed through the thalamus.
description_en: A paired gray-matter structure in the diencephalon that serves as the major relay station for sensory and motor signals to and from the cerebral cortex. Nearly all sensory information (except olfaction) is processed through the thalamus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A localized collection of pus surrounded by inflamed tissue, resulting from bacterial infection. Abscesses require drainage (surgical or spontaneous) to resolve; antibiotics alone are generally insufficient.
description_en: A localized collection of pus surrounded by inflamed tissue, resulting from bacterial infection. Abscesses require drainage (surgical or spontaneous) to resolve; antibiotics alone are generally insufficient.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Abnormal fibrous bands that form between tissue surfaces following inflammation, injury, or surgery. Intra-abdominal adhesions are a leading cause of small bowel obstruction and pelvic pain.
description_en: Abnormal fibrous bands that form between tissue surfaces following inflammation, injury, or surgery. Intra-abdominal adhesions are a leading cause of small bowel obstruction and pelvic pain.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Decrease in the size of a tissue or organ due to loss of cells or reduction in cell size. Atrophy can result from disuse, denervation, inadequate nutrition, or loss of hormonal stimulation.
description_en: Decrease in the size of a tissue or organ due to loss of cells or reduction in cell size. Atrophy can result from disuse, denervation, inadequate nutrition, or loss of hormonal stimulation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in interstitial tissue spaces, causing swelling. Edema can result from increased capillary pressure, decreased plasma proteins, lymphatic obstruction, or increased capillary permeability.
description_en: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in interstitial tissue spaces, causing swelling. Edema can result from increased capillary pressure, decreased plasma proteins, lymphatic obstruction, or increased capillary permeability.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Obstruction of a blood vessel by a mass (embolus) that has traveled from another site in the circulation. Common emboli include blood clots (thromboembolism), fat globules, air bubbles, and amniotic fluid.
description_en: Obstruction of a blood vessel by a mass (embolus) that has traveled from another site in the circulation. Common emboli include blood clots (thromboembolism), fat globules, air bubbles, and amniotic fluid.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An abnormal communication between two epithelium-lined surfaces, such as two organs or between an organ and the skin. Fistulae may arise from infection, inflammation (e.g., Crohn's disease), or trauma and often require surgical repair.
description_en: An abnormal communication between two epithelium-lined surfaces, such as two organs or between an organ and the skin. Fistulae may arise from infection, inflammation (e.g., Crohn's disease), or trauma and often require surgical repair.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Escape of blood from a ruptured blood vessel. Hemorrhage can be classified by location (e.g., intracranial, subarachnoid, gastrointestinal) and is life-threatening when significant volumes are lost rapidly.
description_en: Escape of blood from a ruptured blood vessel. Hemorrhage can be classified by location (e.g., intracranial, subarachnoid, gastrointestinal) and is life-threatening when significant volumes are lost rapidly.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Protrusion of an organ or tissue through an abnormal opening in its containing wall. Intervertebral disc herniation occurs when the nucleus pulposus protrudes through a torn annulus fibrosus, often compressing nearby nerve roots.
description_en: Protrusion of an organ or tissue through an abnormal opening in its containing wall. Intervertebral disc herniation occurs when the nucleus pulposus protrudes through a torn annulus fibrosus, often compressing nearby nerve roots.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Increase in the size of a tissue or organ due to enlargement of its constituent cells. Cardiac hypertrophy occurs in response to chronic pressure overload; skeletal muscle hypertrophy results from exercise.
description_en: Increase in the size of a tissue or organ due to enlargement of its constituent cells. Cardiac hypertrophy occurs in response to chronic pressure overload; skeletal muscle hypertrophy results from exercise.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Tissue necrosis resulting from prolonged ischemia due to obstruction of arterial supply or venous drainage. Myocardial infarction (heart attack) and cerebral infarction (ischemic stroke) are the most clinically significant examples.
description_en: Tissue necrosis resulting from prolonged ischemia due to obstruction of arterial supply or venous drainage. Myocardial infarction (heart attack) and cerebral infarction (ischemic stroke) are the most clinically significant examples.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A protective vascular and cellular response to injury, infection, or irritation characterized by the cardinal signs: redness (rubor), heat (calor), swelling (tumor), pain (dolor), and loss of function (functio laesa). It can be acute or chronic.
description_en: A protective vascular and cellular response to injury, infection, or irritation characterized by the cardinal signs: redness (rubor), heat (calor), swelling (tumor), pain (dolor), and loss of function (functio laesa). It can be acute or chronic.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Insufficient blood supply to a tissue or organ, resulting in oxygen deprivation and potential tissue damage. Prolonged ischemia leads to infarction (tissue death).
description_en: Insufficient blood supply to a tissue or organ, resulting in oxygen deprivation and potential tissue damage. Prolonged ischemia leads to infarction (tissue death).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Relating to or caused by ischemia (insufficient blood supply). The adjective is used in clinical terms such as ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and ischemic colitis to indicate vascular insufficiency as the underlying mechanism.
description_en: Relating to or caused by ischemia (insufficient blood supply). The adjective is used in clinical terms such as ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and ischemic colitis to indicate vascular insufficiency as the underlying mechanism.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The spread of malignant cells from a primary tumor to distant sites via blood vessels, lymphatics, or body cavities, where they form secondary tumors. Metastasis is the primary cause of cancer-related mortality.
description_en: The spread of malignant cells from a primary tumor to distant sites via blood vessels, lymphatics, or body cavities, where they form secondary tumors. Metastasis is the primary cause of cancer-related mortality.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Death of cells or tissues due to injury, disease, or failure of blood supply. Unlike apoptosis (programmed cell death), necrosis is a pathological process that triggers inflammation.
description_en: Death of cells or tissues due to injury, disease, or failure of blood supply. Unlike apoptosis (programmed cell death), necrosis is a pathological process that triggers inflammation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An abnormal mass of tissue resulting from uncontrolled cell proliferation. Neoplasms are classified as benign (non-invasive) or malignant (invasive, capable of metastasis); the term is synonymous with 'tumor' in common clinical usage.
description_en: An abnormal mass of tissue resulting from uncontrolled cell proliferation. Neoplasms are classified as benign (non-invasive) or malignant (invasive, capable of metastasis); the term is synonymous with 'tumor' in common clinical usage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Downward displacement or falling of an organ from its normal position. Mitral valve prolapse, uterine prolapse, and rectal prolapse are common clinical examples, each with distinct anatomical and functional consequences.
description_en: Downward displacement or falling of an organ from its normal position. Mitral valve prolapse, uterine prolapse, and rectal prolapse are common clinical examples, each with distinct anatomical and functional consequences.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A life-threatening systemic inflammatory response to infection in which the body's immune response causes widespread tissue damage. Septic shock is the most severe form, characterized by refractory hypotension and multi-organ failure.
description_en: A life-threatening systemic inflammatory response to infection in which the body's immune response causes widespread tissue damage. Septic shock is the most severe form, characterized by refractory hypotension and multi-organ failure.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Abnormal narrowing of a passage or opening in the body. Vascular stenosis (such as carotid or coronary) restricts blood flow and can cause ischemia.
description_en: Abnormal narrowing of a passage or opening in the body. Vascular stenosis (such as carotid or coronary) restricts blood flow and can cause ischemia.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a blood vessel, obstructing normal blood flow. Thrombosis can occur in arteries (arterial thrombosis) or veins (venous thrombosis, commonly deep vein thrombosis/DVT).
description_en: The formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a blood vessel, obstructing normal blood flow. Thrombosis can occur in arteries (arterial thrombosis) or veins (venous thrombosis, commonly deep vein thrombosis/DVT).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A rounded, knuckle-like articular prominence on a bone. Condyles form part of synovial joint surfaces; examples include the medial and lateral condyles of the femur and the mandibular condyle of the temporomandibular joint.
description_en: A rounded, knuckle-like articular prominence on a bone. Condyles form part of synovial joint surfaces; examples include the medial and lateral condyles of the femur and the mandibular condyle of the temporomandibular joint.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A narrow ridge or raised border along a bone surface. The iliac crest of the pelvis, the tibial crest (shin), and the intertrochanteric crest of the femur are clinically important surface landmarks.
description_en: A narrow ridge or raised border along a bone surface. The iliac crest of the pelvis, the tibial crest (shin), and the intertrochanteric crest of the femur are clinically important surface landmarks.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The shaft or central portion of a long bone, composed primarily of compact cortical bone surrounding a medullary cavity filled with yellow (fat) marrow in adults. It provides rigidity and longitudinal strength.
description_en: The shaft or central portion of a long bone, composed primarily of compact cortical bone surrounding a medullary cavity filled with yellow (fat) marrow in adults. It provides rigidity and longitudinal strength.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A thin vascular membrane lining the inner surface of bone (medullary cavity) and the surfaces of the Haversian canals. It contains osteoblasts and osteoclasts involved in bone remodeling.
description_en: A thin vascular membrane lining the inner surface of bone (medullary cavity) and the surfaces of the Haversian canals. It contains osteoblasts and osteoclasts involved in bone remodeling.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A projection on the surface of a condyle that serves primarily as a site of muscle and ligament attachment rather than articulation. The medial epicondyle of the humerus is a common site of injury (golfer's elbow); the lateral epicondyle is affected in tennis elbow.
description_en: A projection on the surface of a condyle that serves primarily as a site of muscle and ligament attachment rather than articulation. The medial epicondyle of the humerus is a common site of injury (golfer's elbow); the lateral epicondyle is affected in tennis elbow.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The rounded end of a long bone, composed mainly of cancellous (spongy) bone and covered with articular cartilage. The epiphyses develop from secondary ossification centers and are separated from the diaphysis by the epiphyseal plate in growing bone.
description_en: The rounded end of a long bone, composed mainly of cancellous (spongy) bone and covered with articular cartilage. The epiphyses develop from secondary ossification centers and are separated from the diaphysis by the epiphyseal plate in growing bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A small, flat articular surface on a bone. Vertebral facet joints (zygapophyseal joints) allow gliding movements between adjacent vertebrae; costal facets on thoracic vertebrae articulate with the ribs.
description_en: A small, flat articular surface on a bone. Vertebral facet joints (zygapophyseal joints) allow gliding movements between adjacent vertebrae; costal facets on thoracic vertebrae articulate with the ribs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A membranous gap between the incompletely ossified skull bones of a newborn, allowing the cranium to deform during birth and the brain to grow postnatally. The anterior fontanelle (bregma) is the largest and typically closes by 18-24 months of age.
description_en: A membranous gap between the incompletely ossified skull bones of a newborn, allowing the cranium to deform during birth and the brain to grow postnatally. The anterior fontanelle (bregma) is the largest and typically closes by 18-24 months of age.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A natural opening or passage in a bone or other anatomical structure through which nerves, blood vessels, or other structures pass. Examples include the foramen magnum (allowing the brainstem to pass through the skull) and the obturator foramen of the pelvis.
description_en: A natural opening or passage in a bone or other anatomical structure through which nerves, blood vessels, or other structures pass. Examples include the foramen magnum (allowing the brainstem to pass through the skull) and the obturator foramen of the pelvis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A shallow concave depression on the surface of a bone, often serving as an articular surface or as attachment for muscles. Examples include the glenoid fossa of the scapula (shoulder joint socket) and the olecranon fossa of the humerus.
description_en: A shallow concave depression on the surface of a bone, often serving as an articular surface or as attachment for muscles. Examples include the glenoid fossa of the scapula (shoulder joint socket) and the olecranon fossa of the humerus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The structural unit of compact cortical bone, also called an osteon, consisting of concentric lamellae of bone matrix surrounding a central Haversian canal that contains blood vessels and nerves. Multiple osteons give compact bone its characteristic appearance in cross-section.
description_en: The structural unit of compact cortical bone, also called an osteon, consisting of concentric lamellae of bone matrix surrounding a central Haversian canal that contains blood vessels and nerves. Multiple osteons give compact bone its characteristic appearance in cross-section.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The region between the epiphysis and diaphysis of a long bone that contains the epiphyseal plate (growth plate) in growing individuals. After skeletal maturity, the epiphyseal plate ossifies and the metaphysis merges with the diaphysis.
description_en: The region between the epiphysis and diaphysis of a long bone that contains the epiphyseal plate (growth plate) in growing individuals. After skeletal maturity, the epiphyseal plate ossifies and the metaphysis merges with the diaphysis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An indentation or concavity on the edge of a bone. The sciatic notch of the pelvis (greater and lesser) transmits the sciatic nerve and other neurovascular structures; the trochlear notch of the ulna articulates with the humerus.
description_en: An indentation or concavity on the edge of a bone. The sciatic notch of the pelvis (greater and lesser) transmits the sciatic nerve and other neurovascular structures; the trochlear notch of the ulna articulates with the humerus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The process of bone tissue formation. Intramembranous ossification forms flat bones directly from mesenchyme; endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage model with bone, forming most of the axial and appendicular skeleton.
description_en: The process of bone tissue formation. Intramembranous ossification forms flat bones directly from mesenchyme; endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage model with bone, forming most of the axial and appendicular skeleton.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A bone-forming cell derived from mesenchymal stem cells that synthesizes and secretes the organic matrix (osteoid) of bone and regulates its subsequent mineralization with calcium and phosphate. When surrounded by matrix, an osteoblast becomes an osteocyte.
description_en: A bone-forming cell derived from mesenchymal stem cells that synthesizes and secretes the organic matrix (osteoid) of bone and regulates its subsequent mineralization with calcium and phosphate. When surrounded by matrix, an osteoblast becomes an osteocyte.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A large, multinucleated cell derived from hematopoietic monocyte precursors that resorbs bone by secreting hydrochloric acid and proteolytic enzymes into a resorption lacuna (Howship's lacuna). It is the principal cell responsible for bone remodeling and turnover.
description_en: A large, multinucleated cell derived from hematopoietic monocyte precursors that resorbs bone by secreting hydrochloric acid and proteolytic enzymes into a resorption lacuna (Howship's lacuna). It is the principal cell responsible for bone remodeling and turnover.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A mature bone cell enclosed within a lacuna (small cavity) in the bone matrix, connected to neighboring osteocytes and the periosteum via canaliculi (tiny channels) through which nutrients and signals are exchanged. Osteocytes are the most abundant bone cells and act as mechanosensors.
description_en: A mature bone cell enclosed within a lacuna (small cavity) in the bone matrix, connected to neighboring osteocytes and the periosteum via canaliculi (tiny channels) through which nutrients and signals are exchanged. Osteocytes are the most abundant bone cells and act as mechanosensors.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The dense fibrous membrane covering the outer surface of bone except at articular cartilage. The outer fibrous layer provides attachment for tendons and ligaments; the inner osteogenic layer contains osteoblasts essential for bone growth and repair.
description_en: The dense fibrous membrane covering the outer surface of bone except at articular cartilage. The outer fibrous layer provides attachment for tendons and ligaments; the inner osteogenic layer contains osteoblasts essential for bone growth and repair.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Any prominent projection or outgrowth from a bone. Processes serve as attachment sites for muscles and ligaments. Examples include the styloid process of the temporal bone, the coracoid process of the scapula, and the transverse processes of vertebrae.
description_en: Any prominent projection or outgrowth from a bone. Processes serve as attachment sites for muscles and ligaments. Examples include the styloid process of the temporal bone, the coracoid process of the scapula, and the transverse processes of vertebrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A sharp, slender projection of bone, sharper than a tubercle or process. The spine of the scapula divides its posterior surface into supraspinous and infraspinous fossae; vertebral spinous processes are palpable along the back.
description_en: A sharp, slender projection of bone, sharper than a tubercle or process. The spine of the scapula divides its posterior surface into supraspinous and infraspinous fossae; vertebral spinous processes are palpable along the back.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A groove or furrow on the surface of a bone, often accommodating tendons, vessels, or nerves. The intertubercular sulcus (bicipital groove) of the humerus guides the long head of the biceps tendon.
description_en: A groove or furrow on the surface of a bone, often accommodating tendons, vessels, or nerves. The intertubercular sulcus (bicipital groove) of the humerus guides the long head of the biceps tendon.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A fibrous immovable joint between adjacent bones of the skull. Major sutures include the coronal, sagittal, lambdoid, and squamous sutures. Premature fusion of sutures (craniosynostosis) can restrict brain growth.
description_en: A fibrous immovable joint between adjacent bones of the skull. Major sutures include the coronal, sagittal, lambdoid, and squamous sutures. Premature fusion of sutures (craniosynostosis) can restrict brain growth.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A large, blunt, irregular bony prominence found exclusively on the femur. The greater trochanter is the insertion of several hip abductor muscles; the lesser trochanter receives the iliopsoas tendon. Trochanters are important surgical and clinical landmarks.
description_en: A large, blunt, irregular bony prominence found exclusively on the femur. The greater trochanter is the insertion of several hip abductor muscles; the lesser trochanter receives the iliopsoas tendon. Trochanters are important surgical and clinical landmarks.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A large, rough, rounded projection on a bone that serves as an attachment site for tendons and muscles. The tibial tuberosity is the insertion of the patellar tendon (quadriceps femoris); the greater tuberosity of the humerus anchors the rotator cuff.
description_en: A large, rough, rounded projection on a bone that serves as an attachment site for tendons and muscles. The tibial tuberosity is the insertion of the patellar tendon (quadriceps femoris); the greater tuberosity of the humerus anchors the rotator cuff.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Perforating canals that run perpendicular or oblique to the long axis of bone, connecting adjacent Haversian canals, the periosteum, and the endosteum, and conveying blood vessels and nerves. Also called perforating canals.
description_en: Perforating canals that run perpendicular or oblique to the long axis of bone, connecting adjacent Haversian canals, the periosteum, and the endosteum, and conveying blood vessels and nerves. Also called perforating canals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A globular protein that polymerizes to form the thin filaments of the sarcomere. During muscle contraction, myosin cross-bridges bind to actin and pull the thin filaments toward the center of the sarcomere, shortening the muscle.
description_en: A globular protein that polymerizes to form the thin filaments of the sarcomere. During muscle contraction, myosin cross-bridges bind to actin and pull the thin filaments toward the center of the sarcomere, shortening the muscle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The primary muscle responsible for producing a specific movement; also called the prime mover. For elbow flexion, the biceps brachii is the agonist. Agonist activity is coordinated with antagonist inhibition to produce smooth movement.
description_en: The primary muscle responsible for producing a specific movement; also called the prime mover. For elbow flexion, the biceps brachii is the agonist. Agonist activity is coordinated with antagonist inhibition to produce smooth movement.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle that opposes or reverses the action of an agonist. During elbow flexion, the triceps brachii is the antagonist. Antagonists relax to allow movement and contract to decelerate or reverse it.
description_en: A muscle that opposes or reverses the action of an agonist. During elbow flexion, the triceps brachii is the antagonist. Antagonists relax to allow movement and contract to decelerate or reverse it.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A flat, sheet-like tendon that attaches a broad muscle to bone or to another muscle. The external abdominal oblique aponeurosis and the epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica) of the scalp are prominent examples.
description_en: A flat, sheet-like tendon that attaches a broad muscle to bone or to another muscle. The external abdominal oblique aponeurosis and the epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica) of the scalp are prominent examples.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle whose fibers are arranged in concentric rings around an opening (sphincter). Contraction closes the aperture. Examples include the orbicularis oculi (eye), orbicularis oris (mouth), and various sphincters of the gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts.
description_en: A muscle whose fibers are arranged in concentric rings around an opening (sphincter). Contraction closes the aperture. Examples include the orbicularis oculi (eye), orbicularis oris (mouth), and various sphincters of the gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle contraction in which the muscle shortens while under tension, producing movement in the direction of the contracting force. The biceps brachii undergoes concentric contraction when lifting a weight toward the shoulder.
description_en: A muscle contraction in which the muscle shortens while under tension, producing movement in the direction of the contracting force. The biceps brachii undergoes concentric contraction when lifting a weight toward the shoulder.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle in which a broad origin converges onto a narrow insertion, with muscle fibers oriented at varying angles (fan-shaped). The pectoralis major is the classic example; convergent architecture allows the muscle to exert forces from multiple directions.
description_en: A muscle in which a broad origin converges onto a narrow insertion, with muscle fibers oriented at varying angles (fan-shaped). The pectoralis major is the classic example; convergent architecture allows the muscle to exert forces from multiple directions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle contraction in which the muscle lengthens while under tension, decelerating a movement or controlling a load. Eccentric contractions generate the greatest forces and are the most common cause of delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS).
description_en: A muscle contraction in which the muscle lengthens while under tension, decelerating a movement or controlling a load. Eccentric contractions generate the greatest forces and are the most common cause of delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The delicate sheath of connective tissue surrounding each individual muscle fiber (cell). It contains capillaries and nerve terminals that supply the fiber and contributes to the tendon at the muscle's insertion.
description_en: The delicate sheath of connective tissue surrounding each individual muscle fiber (cell). It contains capillaries and nerve terminals that supply the fiber and contributes to the tendon at the muscle's insertion.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outermost connective tissue sheath surrounding an entire skeletal muscle. The epimysium is continuous with the deep fascia and the tendons at both ends of the muscle, and it transmits contractile forces to the skeleton.
description_en: The outermost connective tissue sheath surrounding an entire skeletal muscle. The epimysium is continuous with the deep fascia and the tendons at both ends of the muscle, and it transmits contractile forces to the skeleton.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle that stabilizes the origin of an agonist by anchoring the proximal bone, allowing the agonist to exert its force more efficiently on the distal bone. The scapular stabilizers (serratus anterior, rhomboids) act as fixators during arm movements.
description_en: A muscle that stabilizes the origin of an agonist by anchoring the proximal bone, allowing the agonist to exert its force more efficiently on the distal bone. The scapular stabilizers (serratus anterior, rhomboids) act as fixators during arm movements.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Describing a spindle-shaped muscle with fibers running parallel to the line of pull, tapering at each end into tendons. Fusiform muscles (e.g., biceps brachii) have greater range of contraction but lower force per unit volume compared with pennate muscles.
description_en: Describing a spindle-shaped muscle with fibers running parallel to the line of pull, tapering at each end into tendons. Fusiform muscles (e.g., biceps brachii) have greater range of contraction but lower force per unit volume compared with pennate muscles.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A type of muscle contraction where the muscle generates tension without changing its length. Isometric contractions occur during postural holding and joint stabilization, such as maintaining a plank position.
description_en: A type of muscle contraction where the muscle generates tension without changing its length. Isometric contractions occur during postural holding and joint stabilization, such as maintaining a plank position.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A type of muscle contraction where the muscle changes length while maintaining relatively constant tension. Isotonic contractions are subdivided into concentric (shortening) and eccentric (lengthening) contractions.
description_en: A type of muscle contraction where the muscle changes length while maintaining relatively constant tension. Isotonic contractions are subdivided into concentric (shortening) and eccentric (lengthening) contractions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The specialized region of skeletal muscle fiber membrane (sarcolemma) that forms one side of the neuromuscular junction, containing a high density of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. Binding of acetylcholine generates the end plate potential that triggers muscle contraction.
description_en: The specialized region of skeletal muscle fiber membrane (sarcolemma) that forms one side of the neuromuscular junction, containing a high density of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. Binding of acetylcholine generates the end plate potential that triggers muscle contraction.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A single motor neuron and all the skeletal muscle fibers it innervates. All fibers of a motor unit contract together (all-or-none principle). Fine motor control (e.g., eye muscles) uses small units with few fibers; postural muscles use larger units.
description_en: A single motor neuron and all the skeletal muscle fibers it innervates. All fibers of a motor unit contract together (all-or-none principle). Fine motor control (e.g., eye muscles) uses small units with few fibers; postural muscles use larger units.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cylindrical bundle of contractile proteins (actin and myosin) running the length of a muscle fiber. Each muscle cell (fiber) contains hundreds of parallel myofibrils, which in turn contain thousands of sarcomeres in series.
description_en: A cylindrical bundle of contractile proteins (actin and myosin) running the length of a muscle fiber. Each muscle cell (fiber) contains hundreds of parallel myofibrils, which in turn contain thousands of sarcomeres in series.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The molecular motor protein forming the thick filaments of the sarcomere. Myosin heads hydrolyze ATP to generate the power stroke that moves actin filaments, producing force and shortening. It is the most abundant protein in muscle tissue.
description_en: The molecular motor protein forming the thick filaments of the sarcomere. Myosin heads hydrolyze ATP to generate the power stroke that moves actin filaments, producing force and shortening. It is the most abundant protein in muscle tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The chemical synapse between a motor neuron's axon terminal and a skeletal muscle fiber's motor end plate. Acetylcholine released into the synaptic cleft binds receptors to trigger an action potential and muscle contraction; it is the site of action of neuromuscular blocking agents and botulinum toxin.
description_en: The chemical synapse between a motor neuron's axon terminal and a skeletal muscle fiber's motor end plate. Acetylcholine released into the synaptic cleft binds receptors to trigger an action potential and muscle contraction; it is the site of action of neuromuscular blocking agents and botulinum toxin.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Describing a muscle fiber arrangement in which fibers are oriented at an angle to the line of pull (like a feather — Latin: penna). Pennate muscles (unipennate, bipennate, multipennate) pack more fibers into a given volume, generating greater force than parallel-fiber muscles of the same size.
description_en: Describing a muscle fiber arrangement in which fibers are oriented at an angle to the line of pull (like a feather — Latin: penna). Pennate muscles (unipennate, bipennate, multipennate) pack more fibers into a given volume, generating greater force than parallel-fiber muscles of the same size.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A layer of connective tissue that bundles groups of muscle fibers into fascicles. The perimysium contains blood vessels and nerves that supply the fascicle and is thicker than the endomysium.
description_en: A layer of connective tissue that bundles groups of muscle fibers into fascicles. The perimysium contains blood vessels and nerves that supply the fascicle and is thicker than the endomysium.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The muscle primarily responsible for a specific action at a joint; synonymous with agonist. In shoulder abduction, the deltoid is the prime mover, while the supraspinatus initiates and assists the movement.
description_en: The muscle primarily responsible for a specific action at a joint; synonymous with agonist. In shoulder abduction, the deltoid is the prime mover, while the supraspinatus initiates and assists the movement.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A band of thickened deep fascia that holds tendons in place as they cross a joint, preventing bowstringing during movement. The flexor and extensor retinacula at the wrist and ankle are clinically important; carpal tunnel syndrome occurs within the flexor retinaculum.
description_en: A band of thickened deep fascia that holds tendons in place as they cross a joint, preventing bowstringing during movement. The flexor and extensor retinacula at the wrist and ankle are clinically important; carpal tunnel syndrome occurs within the flexor retinaculum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The basic contractile unit of a skeletal muscle fiber, bounded by two Z-discs. It contains overlapping thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filaments; sliding of these filaments past each other produces muscle shortening according to the sliding filament theory.
description_en: The basic contractile unit of a skeletal muscle fiber, bounded by two Z-discs. It contains overlapping thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filaments; sliding of these filaments past each other produces muscle shortening according to the sliding filament theory.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A muscle that assists the agonist in performing a movement or that stabilizes a joint to make the agonist more effective. Synergists reduce unnecessary motion and increase the efficiency of the prime mover.
description_en: A muscle that assists the agonist in performing a movement or that stabilizes a joint to make the agonist more effective. Synergists reduce unnecessary motion and increase the efficiency of the prime mover.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A tiny, thin-walled air sac at the terminus of the bronchiolar tree where gas exchange occurs. The human lungs contain approximately 300-500 million alveoli, providing a total surface area of about 70 square meters for oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange.
description_en: A tiny, thin-walled air sac at the terminus of the bronchiolar tree where gas exchange occurs. The human lungs contain approximately 300-500 million alveoli, providing a total surface area of about 70 square meters for oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A small airway less than 1 mm in diameter that lacks cartilage in its walls, relying instead on smooth muscle to regulate airway diameter. Terminal bronchioles lead to respiratory bronchioles and ultimately to alveolar ducts; their smooth muscle is the target of bronchodilator therapy in asthma.
description_en: A small airway less than 1 mm in diameter that lacks cartilage in its walls, relying instead on smooth muscle to regulate airway diameter. Terminal bronchioles lead to respiratory bronchioles and ultimately to alveolar ducts; their smooth muscle is the target of bronchodilator therapy in asthma.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A large cartilage-reinforced airway of the conducting zone. The trachea divides into the right and left main (primary) bronchi, which subdivide into lobar (secondary) and segmental (tertiary) bronchi supplying each bronchopulmonary segment.
description_en: A large cartilage-reinforced airway of the conducting zone. The trachea divides into the right and left main (primary) bronchi, which subdivide into lobar (secondary) and segmental (tertiary) bronchi supplying each bronchopulmonary segment.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The volume of air that occupies the conducting airways and does not participate in gas exchange. Anatomical dead space (~150 mL) is the volume in the trachea, bronchi, and bronchioles; physiological dead space also includes non-perfused alveoli.
description_en: The volume of air that occupies the conducting airways and does not participate in gas exchange. Anatomical dead space (~150 mL) is the volume in the trachea, bronchi, and bronchioles; physiological dead space also includes non-perfused alveoli.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The dome-shaped musculotendinous sheet separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities. It is the principal muscle of inspiration; when it contracts, it flattens and descends, increasing thoracic volume and drawing air into the lungs.
description_en: The dome-shaped musculotendinous sheet separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities. It is the principal muscle of inspiration; when it contracts, it flattens and descends, increasing thoracic volume and drawing air into the lungs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The diffusion of oxygen from alveolar air into pulmonary capillary blood, and of carbon dioxide in the reverse direction, driven by partial pressure gradients. Efficient gas exchange depends on a thin alveolar-capillary membrane, adequate surface area, and matched ventilation and perfusion.
description_en: The diffusion of oxygen from alveolar air into pulmonary capillary blood, and of carbon dioxide in the reverse direction, driven by partial pressure gradients. Efficient gas exchange depends on a thin alveolar-capillary membrane, adequate surface area, and matched ventilation and perfusion.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cartilaginous structure in the anterior neck (C3-C6) that connects the pharynx to the trachea. It houses the vocal folds (cords) for phonation, serves as the entrance to the lower airways, and contains the epiglottis, which prevents aspiration during swallowing.
description_en: A cartilaginous structure in the anterior neck (C3-C6) that connects the pharynx to the trachea. It houses the vocal folds (cords) for phonation, serves as the entrance to the lower airways, and contains the epiglottis, which prevents aspiration during swallowing.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A fibromuscular tube behind the nasal and oral cavities that serves as a common passage for food and air. It is divided into the nasopharynx (posterior to the nasal cavity), oropharynx (posterior to the oral cavity), and laryngopharynx (hypopharynx).
description_en: A fibromuscular tube behind the nasal and oral cavities that serves as a common passage for food and air. It is divided into the nasopharynx (posterior to the nasal cavity), oropharynx (posterior to the oral cavity), and laryngopharynx (hypopharynx).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The serous membrane enveloping each lung. The visceral pleura covers the lung surface; the parietal pleura lines the thoracic wall, diaphragm, and mediastinum. The two layers are continuous at the lung hilum.
description_en: The serous membrane enveloping each lung. The visceral pleura covers the lung surface; the parietal pleura lines the thoracic wall, diaphragm, and mediastinum. The two layers are continuous at the lung hilum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The potential space between the visceral and parietal pleural layers containing a small amount of serous fluid that reduces friction during breathing. A pneumothorax occurs when air enters this space, causing lung collapse.
description_en: The potential space between the visceral and parietal pleural layers containing a small amount of serous fluid that reduces friction during breathing. A pneumothorax occurs when air enters this space, causing lung collapse.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A complex mixture of phospholipids and proteins (primarily dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine) secreted by Type II pneumocytes that reduces alveolar surface tension, preventing alveolar collapse at end-expiration. Deficiency causes respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants.
description_en: A complex mixture of phospholipids and proteins (primarily dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine) secreted by Type II pneumocytes that reduces alveolar surface tension, preventing alveolar collapse at end-expiration. Deficiency causes respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The volume of air inhaled or exhaled in a single normal, quiet breath, approximately 500 mL in a healthy adult. Tidal volume multiplied by breathing rate equals minute ventilation, a key measure of respiratory function.
description_en: The volume of air inhaled or exhaled in a single normal, quiet breath, approximately 500 mL in a healthy adult. Tidal volume multiplied by breathing rate equals minute ventilation, a key measure of respiratory function.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The cartilaginous and membranous tube extending from the larynx (at the level of C6) to the carina (at T4-T5) where it divides into the two main bronchi. It is supported by 16-20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings that prevent collapse.
description_en: The cartilaginous and membranous tube extending from the larynx (at the level of C6) to the carina (at T4-T5) where it divides into the two main bronchi. It is supported by 16-20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings that prevent collapse.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The mechanical process of moving air in and out of the lungs through the respiratory tract. Pulmonary ventilation is driven by pressure differences created by respiratory muscle activity and is distinct from gas exchange (respiration at the alveolar level).
description_en: The mechanical process of moving air in and out of the lungs through the respiratory tract. Pulmonary ventilation is driven by pressure differences created by respiratory muscle activity and is distinct from gas exchange (respiration at the alveolar level).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after a maximal inhalation, equal to the sum of tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, and expiratory reserve volume. It is approximately 4.5-5 L in a healthy adult and is reduced in restrictive lung diseases.
description_en: The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after a maximal inhalation, equal to the sum of tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, and expiratory reserve volume. It is approximately 4.5-5 L in a healthy adult and is reduced in restrictive lung diseases.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cluster of secretory cells (acinar cells) in the exocrine pancreas that produce and secrete digestive enzymes (including amylase, lipase, and proteases) into a central lumen that drains into the pancreatic duct system. Acinar cells are vulnerable to autodigestion in pancreatitis.
description_en: A cluster of secretory cells (acinar cells) in the exocrine pancreas that produce and secrete digestive enzymes (including amylase, lipase, and proteases) into a central lumen that drains into the pancreatic duct system. Acinar cells are vulnerable to autodigestion in pancreatitis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A yellow-green alkaline fluid produced by hepatocytes and stored in the gallbladder. It contains bile salts, bilirubin, cholesterol, phospholipids, and electrolytes. Bile salts emulsify dietary fats in the small intestine to facilitate enzymatic digestion and absorption.
description_en: A yellow-green alkaline fluid produced by hepatocytes and stored in the gallbladder. It contains bile salts, bilirubin, cholesterol, phospholipids, and electrolytes. Bile salts emulsify dietary fats in the small intestine to facilitate enzymatic digestion and absorption.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The sac-like pouches of the large intestine formed by contraction of the taeniae coli, giving the colon its characteristic segmented appearance on imaging. Haustral contractions slowly mix colonic contents and absorb water.
