description_en: The sac-like pouches of the large intestine formed by contraction of the taeniae coli, giving the colon its characteristic segmented appearance on imaging. Haustral contractions slowly mix colonic contents and absorb water.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The basic structural and functional unit of the liver, roughly hexagonal in shape, consisting of hepatocytes arranged in plates radiating from a central vein, with portal triads (portal vein branch, hepatic artery branch, bile duct) at each corner. Blood flows from the portal triads inward to the central vein.
description_en: The basic structural and functional unit of the liver, roughly hexagonal in shape, consisting of hepatocytes arranged in plates radiating from a central vein, with portal triads (portal vein branch, hepatic artery branch, bile duct) at each corner. Blood flows from the portal triads inward to the central vein.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Clusters of endocrine cells scattered throughout the exocrine pancreatic tissue, comprising approximately 1-2% of pancreatic volume. They contain alpha cells (glucagon), beta cells (insulin), delta cells (somatostatin), and PP cells, regulating blood glucose homeostasis.
description_en: Clusters of endocrine cells scattered throughout the exocrine pancreatic tissue, comprising approximately 1-2% of pancreatic volume. They contain alpha cells (glucagon), beta cells (insulin), delta cells (somatostatin), and PP cells, regulating blood glucose homeostasis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A double fold of peritoneum that attaches the small intestine to the posterior abdominal wall and carries the blood vessels, lymphatics, and nerves supplying the gut. Once considered multiple separate structures, the mesentery is now recognized as a single continuous organ.
description_en: A double fold of peritoneum that attaches the small intestine to the posterior abdominal wall and carries the blood vessels, lymphatics, and nerves supplying the gut. Once considered multiple separate structures, the mesentery is now recognized as a single continuous organ.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Microscopic projections on the apical surface of enterocytes (intestinal absorptive cells) that form the brush border, further amplifying the absorptive surface by approximately 600-fold. They contain digestive enzymes including lactase, sucrase, and maltase.
description_en: Microscopic projections on the apical surface of enterocytes (intestinal absorptive cells) that form the brush border, further amplifying the absorptive surface by approximately 600-fold. They contain digestive enzymes including lactase, sucrase, and maltase.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An apron-like fold of peritoneum attached to the stomach and transverse colon. The greater omentum drapes over the abdominal organs and contains fat; the lesser omentum connects the stomach and duodenum to the liver. The omentum limits the spread of intraperitoneal infection.
description_en: An apron-like fold of peritoneum attached to the stomach and transverse colon. The greater omentum drapes over the abdominal organs and contains fat; the lesser omentum connects the stomach and duodenum to the liver. The omentum limits the spread of intraperitoneal infection.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Coordinated, sequential smooth muscle contractions and relaxations that propel ingested material along the gastrointestinal tract. It is initiated by the enteric nervous system and can occur independently of the central nervous system.
description_en: Coordinated, sequential smooth muscle contractions and relaxations that propel ingested material along the gastrointestinal tract. It is initiated by the enteric nervous system and can occur independently of the central nervous system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The serous membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering most of the abdominal organs. The parietal peritoneum lines the cavity wall; the visceral peritoneum covers organs. The peritoneal cavity normally contains only a small amount of lubricating fluid.
description_en: The serous membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering most of the abdominal organs. The parietal peritoneum lines the cavity wall; the visceral peritoneum covers organs. The peritoneal cavity normally contains only a small amount of lubricating fluid.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Describing organs located behind the parietal peritoneum in the retroperitoneal space. Primary retroperitoneal organs (kidneys, adrenal glands, aorta, IVC) were never suspended by mesentery; secondary retroperitoneal organs (duodenum, pancreas, ascending/descending colon) became retroperitoneal during embryonic development.
description_en: Describing organs located behind the parietal peritoneum in the retroperitoneal space. Primary retroperitoneal organs (kidneys, adrenal glands, aorta, IVC) were never suspended by mesentery; secondary retroperitoneal organs (duodenum, pancreas, ascending/descending colon) became retroperitoneal during embryonic development.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Large longitudinal folds in the mucosa of the stomach that allow the organ to distend when filled with food. Rugae are most prominent in the empty stomach and flatten as the stomach fills, increasing capacity to approximately 1-1.5 L.
description_en: Large longitudinal folds in the mucosa of the stomach that allow the organ to distend when filled with food. Rugae are most prominent in the empty stomach and flatten as the stomach fills, increasing capacity to approximately 1-1.5 L.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A ring of smooth or skeletal muscle that controls the passage of material through a tubular structure. Key GI sphincters include the lower esophageal sphincter (preventing reflux), pyloric sphincter (regulating gastric emptying), and internal/external anal sphincters.
description_en: A ring of smooth or skeletal muscle that controls the passage of material through a tubular structure. Key GI sphincters include the lower esophageal sphincter (preventing reflux), pyloric sphincter (regulating gastric emptying), and internal/external anal sphincters.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Three distinct longitudinal bands of the outer smooth muscle layer that run along the length of the large intestine (except the rectum and appendix). Their continuous tonic contraction gathers the colon into haustra. The three taeniae converge at the base of the appendix, serving as a surgical landmark.
description_en: Three distinct longitudinal bands of the outer smooth muscle layer that run along the length of the large intestine (except the rectum and appendix). Their continuous tonic contraction gathers the colon into haustra. The three taeniae converge at the base of the appendix, serving as a surgical landmark.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Finger-like projections of the small intestinal mucosa (approximately 0.5-1.6 mm tall) that dramatically increase the absorptive surface area of the intestine. Each villus contains a central lacteal for fat absorption and a capillary network for nutrient absorption.
description_en: Finger-like projections of the small intestinal mucosa (approximately 0.5-1.6 mm tall) that dramatically increase the absorptive surface area of the intestine. Each villus contains a central lacteal for fat absorption and a capillary network for nutrient absorption.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outer region of the adrenal gland, divided into three zones: zona glomerulosa (mineralocorticoids, primarily aldosterone), zona fasciculata (glucocorticoids, primarily cortisol), and zona reticularis (androgens). It is derived from mesoderm.
description_en: The outer region of the adrenal gland, divided into three zones: zona glomerulosa (mineralocorticoids, primarily aldosterone), zona fasciculata (glucocorticoids, primarily cortisol), and zona reticularis (androgens). It is derived from mesoderm.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The inner region of the adrenal gland, composed of chromaffin cells derived from neural crest. It secretes catecholamines (primarily epinephrine and norepinephrine) in response to sympathetic stimulation, mediating the 'fight-or-flight' response.
description_en: The inner region of the adrenal gland, composed of chromaffin cells derived from neural crest. It secretes catecholamines (primarily epinephrine and norepinephrine) in response to sympathetic stimulation, mediating the 'fight-or-flight' response.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The primary reproductive endocrine organs: testes in males and ovaries in females. Gonads produce steroid sex hormones (testosterone, estrogen, progesterone) under pituitary FSH and LH control, and produce gametes (sperm and ova).
description_en: The primary reproductive endocrine organs: testes in males and ovaries in females. Gonads produce steroid sex hormones (testosterone, estrogen, progesterone) under pituitary FSH and LH control, and produce gametes (sperm and ova).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A chemical messenger secreted by endocrine cells into the bloodstream that exerts regulatory effects on distant target cells bearing specific receptors. Hormones are classified as amino acid-derived, peptide/protein, or steroid, each with distinct mechanisms of action.
description_en: A chemical messenger secreted by endocrine cells into the bloodstream that exerts regulatory effects on distant target cells bearing specific receptors. Hormones are classified as amino acid-derived, peptide/protein, or steroid, each with distinct mechanisms of action.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The diencephalic region that integrates the nervous and endocrine systems by producing releasing and inhibiting hormones that control anterior pituitary secretion, and by synthesizing oxytocin and ADH for posterior pituitary release. It is the supreme regulator of the endocrine system.
description_en: The diencephalic region that integrates the nervous and endocrine systems by producing releasing and inhibiting hormones that control anterior pituitary secretion, and by synthesizing oxytocin and ADH for posterior pituitary release. It is the supreme regulator of the endocrine system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A regulatory mechanism in which the output of a physiological system inhibits its own production, maintaining homeostasis. The hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis is a classic example: high thyroid hormone levels suppress TSH and TRH secretion.
description_en: A regulatory mechanism in which the output of a physiological system inhibits its own production, maintaining homeostasis. The hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis is a classic example: high thyroid hormone levels suppress TSH and TRH secretion.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The endocrine component of the pancreas (Islets of Langerhans) that regulates blood glucose homeostasis. Beta cells secrete insulin (lowering blood glucose); alpha cells secrete glucagon (raising blood glucose); delta cells secrete somatostatin (inhibiting both).
description_en: The endocrine component of the pancreas (Islets of Langerhans) that regulates blood glucose homeostasis. Beta cells secrete insulin (lowering blood glucose); alpha cells secrete glucagon (raising blood glucose); delta cells secrete somatostatin (inhibiting both).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Four small glands embedded on the posterior surface of the thyroid that secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH), the principal regulator of calcium and phosphate homeostasis. PTH raises blood calcium by stimulating bone resorption, renal calcium reabsorption, and renal activation of vitamin D.
description_en: Four small glands embedded on the posterior surface of the thyroid that secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH), the principal regulator of calcium and phosphate homeostasis. PTH raises blood calcium by stimulating bone resorption, renal calcium reabsorption, and renal activation of vitamin D.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A small pine cone-shaped endocrine gland in the epithalamus that produces melatonin, a hormone regulating circadian rhythms and the sleep-wake cycle. Melatonin secretion is inhibited by light and peaks during darkness.
description_en: A small pine cone-shaped endocrine gland in the epithalamus that produces melatonin, a hormone regulating circadian rhythms and the sleep-wake cycle. Melatonin secretion is inhibited by light and peaks during darkness.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A pea-sized endocrine gland suspended from the hypothalamus by the infundibulum and housed in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone. The anterior pituitary secretes GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, and prolactin; the posterior pituitary releases oxytocin and ADH (vasopressin).
description_en: A pea-sized endocrine gland suspended from the hypothalamus by the infundibulum and housed in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone. The anterior pituitary secretes GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, and prolactin; the posterior pituitary releases oxytocin and ADH (vasopressin).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A regulatory mechanism in which the output of a system amplifies further production, driving the system away from equilibrium until a threshold is reached. The pre-ovulatory LH surge driven by rising estrogen is a key endocrine example; oxytocin during childbirth is another.
description_en: A regulatory mechanism in which the output of a system amplifies further production, driving the system away from equilibrium until a threshold is reached. The pre-ovulatory LH surge driven by rising estrogen is a key endocrine example; oxytocin during childbirth is another.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A protein on or within a target cell that binds a specific hormone or signaling molecule and initiates a biological response. Cell-surface receptors (for peptide hormones) use second messengers; intracellular receptors (for steroid hormones) directly regulate gene transcription.
description_en: A protein on or within a target cell that binds a specific hormone or signaling molecule and initiates a biological response. Cell-surface receptors (for peptide hormones) use second messengers; intracellular receptors (for steroid hormones) directly regulate gene transcription.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A cell that possesses specific receptors for a particular hormone and responds to it. Specificity of endocrine signaling depends on receptor expression rather than hormone distribution, as hormones circulate throughout the body but affect only cells with appropriate receptors.
description_en: A cell that possesses specific receptors for a particular hormone and responds to it. Specificity of endocrine signaling depends on receptor expression rather than hormone distribution, as hormones circulate throughout the body but affect only cells with appropriate receptors.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A bilobed lymphoid and endocrine organ in the anterior mediastinum that is most active in childhood and involutes after puberty. It is essential for T-lymphocyte maturation and secretes thymosin hormones that promote T-cell differentiation.
description_en: A bilobed lymphoid and endocrine organ in the anterior mediastinum that is most active in childhood and involutes after puberty. It is essential for T-lymphocyte maturation and secretes thymosin hormones that promote T-cell differentiation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A bilobed endocrine gland in the anterior neck that produces thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) regulating metabolic rate, growth, and development, and calcitonin regulating calcium homeostasis. It is the largest pure endocrine gland in the body.
description_en: A bilobed endocrine gland in the anterior neck that produces thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) regulating metabolic rate, growth, and development, and calcitonin regulating calcium homeostasis. It is the largest pure endocrine gland in the body.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A specialized loose connective tissue composed predominantly of lipid-filled adipocytes. White adipose tissue stores energy, cushions organs, and provides thermal insulation; brown adipose tissue (more prominent in infants) generates heat via non-shivering thermogenesis.
description_en: A specialized loose connective tissue composed predominantly of lipid-filled adipocytes. White adipose tissue stores energy, cushions organs, and provides thermal insulation; brown adipose tissue (more prominent in infants) generates heat via non-shivering thermogenesis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A loose connective tissue with a loosely woven mesh of collagen, elastic, and reticular fibers embedded in abundant ground substance, containing fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells. It is the most widely distributed connective tissue, forming the packaging material of the body.
description_en: A loose connective tissue with a loosely woven mesh of collagen, elastic, and reticular fibers embedded in abundant ground substance, containing fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells. It is the most widely distributed connective tissue, forming the packaging material of the body.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A specialized fluid connective tissue consisting of formed elements (erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets) suspended in a liquid extracellular matrix (plasma). Blood transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products and mediates immune and hemostatic responses.
description_en: A specialized fluid connective tissue consisting of formed elements (erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets) suspended in a liquid extracellular matrix (plasma). Blood transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products and mediates immune and hemostatic responses.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A specialized connective tissue with a mineralized extracellular matrix of hydroxyapatite (calcium phosphate crystals) embedded in an organic collagen framework, giving it exceptional compressive and tensile strength. Bone tissue is organized as compact (cortical) or spongy (cancellous) bone.
description_en: A specialized connective tissue with a mineralized extracellular matrix of hydroxyapatite (calcium phosphate crystals) embedded in an organic collagen framework, giving it exceptional compressive and tensile strength. Bone tissue is organized as compact (cortical) or spongy (cancellous) bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A rigid but flexible avascular connective tissue composed of chondrocytes embedded in an extracellular matrix of collagen and proteoglycans (primarily aggrecan). It covers articular surfaces, forms the growth plates, and provides structural support in the ear and nose.
description_en: A rigid but flexible avascular connective tissue composed of chondrocytes embedded in an extracellular matrix of collagen and proteoglycans (primarily aggrecan). It covers articular surfaces, forms the growth plates, and provides structural support in the ear and nose.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Describing epithelial cells that are taller than they are wide, with an oval nucleus typically located in the basal region. Simple columnar epithelium lines most of the GI tract and is specialized for absorption; pseudostratified columnar epithelium lines the respiratory tract.
description_en: Describing epithelial cells that are taller than they are wide, with an oval nucleus typically located in the basal region. Simple columnar epithelium lines most of the GI tract and is specialized for absorption; pseudostratified columnar epithelium lines the respiratory tract.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The most abundant and widely distributed of the four primary tissue types, characterized by cells embedded in a large extracellular matrix of fibers (collagen, elastic, reticular) and ground substance. It supports, connects, and protects other tissues and organs.
description_en: The most abundant and widely distributed of the four primary tissue types, characterized by cells embedded in a large extracellular matrix of fibers (collagen, elastic, reticular) and ground substance. It supports, connects, and protects other tissues and organs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Describing epithelial cells that are approximately equal in height and width (cube-shaped), with a centrally placed nucleus. Simple cuboidal epithelium lines kidney tubules and small gland ducts where it specializes in secretion and absorption.
description_en: Describing epithelial cells that are approximately equal in height and width (cube-shaped), with a centrally placed nucleus. Simple cuboidal epithelium lines kidney tubules and small gland ducts where it specializes in secretion and absorption.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A type of dense connective tissue in which collagen fibers are randomly interwoven in multiple planes, providing strength in all directions. It forms the dermis of the skin, joint capsules, and the fibrous periosteum.
description_en: A type of dense connective tissue in which collagen fibers are randomly interwoven in multiple planes, providing strength in all directions. It forms the dermis of the skin, joint capsules, and the fibrous periosteum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A type of dense connective tissue in which collagen fibers are arranged in parallel bundles, giving high tensile strength in one direction. Tendons and ligaments are composed of dense regular connective tissue.
description_en: A type of dense connective tissue in which collagen fibers are arranged in parallel bundles, giving high tensile strength in one direction. Tendons and ligaments are composed of dense regular connective tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A flexible cartilage containing abundant elastic fibers in addition to type II collagen, giving it resilience and the ability to withstand repeated bending. Found in the auricle (outer ear), epiglottis, and Eustachian tube.
description_en: A flexible cartilage containing abundant elastic fibers in addition to type II collagen, giving it resilience and the ability to withstand repeated bending. Found in the auricle (outer ear), epiglottis, and Eustachian tube.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A specialized connective tissue rich in elastin fibers that allows structures to stretch and recoil. Found in the walls of large arteries (allowing them to dampen pulsatile blood flow), the trachea, and the ligamentum flavum of the vertebral column.
description_en: A specialized connective tissue rich in elastin fibers that allows structures to stretch and recoil. Found in the walls of large arteries (allowing them to dampen pulsatile blood flow), the trachea, and the ligamentum flavum of the vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: One of the four primary tissue types, consisting of tightly packed cells with little extracellular matrix that cover body surfaces, line body cavities, and form glands. Epithelium is avascular and is classified by cell shape and number of layers.
description_en: One of the four primary tissue types, consisting of tightly packed cells with little extracellular matrix that cover body surfaces, line body cavities, and form glands. Epithelium is avascular and is classified by cell shape and number of layers.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A tough cartilage containing abundant type I collagen bundles in addition to type II collagen and proteoglycans, combining the tensile strength of dense connective tissue with the compressive resistance of cartilage. Found in intervertebral discs, the pubic symphysis, and menisci.
description_en: A tough cartilage containing abundant type I collagen bundles in addition to type II collagen and proteoglycans, combining the tensile strength of dense connective tissue with the compressive resistance of cartilage. Found in intervertebral discs, the pubic symphysis, and menisci.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The most common type of cartilage, with a glassy, homogeneous matrix rich in type II collagen and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans. It covers articular surfaces (articular cartilage), forms the costal cartilages, the tracheal rings, and the fetal skeleton template.
description_en: The most common type of cartilage, with a glassy, homogeneous matrix rich in type II collagen and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans. It covers articular surfaces (articular cartilage), forms the costal cartilages, the tracheal rings, and the fetal skeleton template.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A loose connective tissue composed of a network of reticular fibers (fine type III collagen) secreted by reticular cells, forming the supportive stroma of lymphoid organs, bone marrow, the liver, and the spleen.
description_en: A loose connective tissue composed of a network of reticular fibers (fine type III collagen) secreted by reticular cells, forming the supportive stroma of lymphoid organs, bone marrow, the liver, and the spleen.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An epithelium consisting of a single layer of cells, all in contact with the basement membrane. It is adapted for absorption and secretion in areas where mechanical stress is low, such as the intestinal lining and kidney tubules.
description_en: An epithelium consisting of a single layer of cells, all in contact with the basement membrane. It is adapted for absorption and secretion in areas where mechanical stress is low, such as the intestinal lining and kidney tubules.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Describing flat, scale-like epithelial cells. Simple squamous epithelium lines blood vessels (endothelium), body cavities (mesothelium), and the alveoli. Stratified squamous epithelium covers skin, oral mucosa, and the esophagus.
description_en: Describing flat, scale-like epithelial cells. Simple squamous epithelium lines blood vessels (endothelium), body cavities (mesothelium), and the alveoli. Stratified squamous epithelium covers skin, oral mucosa, and the esophagus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: An epithelium consisting of multiple cell layers, with only the basal layer contacting the basement membrane. It is found in areas subject to mechanical stress such as the skin (stratified squamous keratinized) and the oral mucosa.
description_en: An epithelium consisting of multiple cell layers, with only the basal layer contacting the basement membrane. It is found in areas subject to mechanical stress such as the skin (stratified squamous keratinized) and the oral mucosa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A stratified epithelium unique to the urinary tract (renal pelvis, ureters, bladder) that can stretch and change shape as the organ fills and empties. Also called urothelium, its surface cells (umbrella cells) are large and dome-shaped when relaxed.
description_en: A stratified epithelium unique to the urinary tract (renal pelvis, ureters, bladder) that can stretch and change shape as the organ fills and empties. Also called urothelium, its surface cells (umbrella cells) are large and dome-shaped when relaxed.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A thin extraembryonic membrane of ectodermal and mesodermal origin that encloses the embryo and fetus in a fluid-filled amniotic cavity. Amniotic fluid cushions the fetus, prevents adhesions, and allows fetal movement. Oligohydramnios (too little fluid) and polyhydramnios (too much) have clinical significance.
description_en: A thin extraembryonic membrane of ectodermal and mesodermal origin that encloses the embryo and fetus in a fluid-filled amniotic cavity. Amniotic fluid cushions the fetus, prevents adhesions, and allows fetal movement. Oligohydramnios (too little fluid) and polyhydramnios (too much) have clinical significance.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The stage of human embryonic development (approximately day 5-6) consisting of a hollow sphere: an outer cell mass (trophoblast) that will form the placenta and extraembryonic membranes, and an inner cell mass (embryoblast) that will form the embryo proper. Implantation of the blastocyst into the uterine endometrium occurs around day 6-10.
description_en: The stage of human embryonic development (approximately day 5-6) consisting of a hollow sphere: an outer cell mass (trophoblast) that will form the placenta and extraembryonic membranes, and an inner cell mass (embryoblast) that will form the embryo proper. Implantation of the blastocyst into the uterine endometrium occurs around day 6-10.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outermost of the three primary germ layers of the embryo, formed during gastrulation. It gives rise to the epidermis and its derivatives (hair, nails, sweat glands), the nervous system (via neurulation), and the special sense organs.
description_en: The outermost of the three primary germ layers of the embryo, formed during gastrulation. It gives rise to the epidermis and its derivatives (hair, nails, sweat glands), the nervous system (via neurulation), and the special sense organs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The innermost of the three primary germ layers. It gives rise to the epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal tract, the respiratory tract, the urinary bladder, and the parenchyma of organs such as the liver, pancreas, and thyroid gland.
description_en: The innermost of the three primary germ layers. It gives rise to the epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal tract, the respiratory tract, the urinary bladder, and the parenchyma of organs such as the liver, pancreas, and thyroid gland.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The fundamental embryonic process (occurring during week 3 in humans) by which the bilaminar embryonic disc is converted into a trilaminar disc through formation of the primitive streak and migration of epiblast cells to form mesoderm and endoderm. It establishes the three primary germ layers.
description_en: The fundamental embryonic process (occurring during week 3 in humans) by which the bilaminar embryonic disc is converted into a trilaminar disc through formation of the primitive streak and migration of epiblast cells to form mesoderm and endoderm. It establishes the three primary germ layers.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The middle of the three primary germ layers, situated between ectoderm and endoderm. It gives rise to muscle, bone, cartilage, connective tissue, the cardiovascular system, the kidneys, and the gonads.
description_en: The middle of the three primary germ layers, situated between ectoderm and endoderm. It gives rise to muscle, bone, cartilage, connective tissue, the cardiovascular system, the kidneys, and the gonads.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A transient population of multipotent cells arising at the lateral margins of the neural plate that migrate extensively and give rise to a diverse array of structures including peripheral neurons and glia, melanocytes, adrenal medullary cells, craniofacial bones and cartilage, and cardiac outflow tract structures.
description_en: A transient population of multipotent cells arising at the lateral margins of the neural plate that migrate extensively and give rise to a diverse array of structures including peripheral neurons and glia, melanocytes, adrenal medullary cells, craniofacial bones and cartilage, and cardiac outflow tract structures.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The embryonic precursor to the central nervous system, formed when the flat neural plate of ectoderm rolls up and closes during neurulation (weeks 3-4 of development). The cranial portion forms the brain; the caudal portion forms the spinal cord. Failure to close causes neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly.
description_en: The embryonic precursor to the central nervous system, formed when the flat neural plate of ectoderm rolls up and closes during neurulation (weeks 3-4 of development). The cranial portion forms the brain; the caudal portion forms the spinal cord. Failure to close causes neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The process (weeks 3-4) by which the neural plate, induced by the notochord, folds to form the neural tube. Cranial portions close first; failure at specific closure sites produces neural tube defects. Adequate maternal folate is essential for neural tube closure.
description_en: The process (weeks 3-4) by which the neural plate, induced by the notochord, folds to form the neural tube. Cranial portions close first; failure at specific closure sites produces neural tube defects. Adequate maternal folate is essential for neural tube closure.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: A rod-like structure of mesodermal origin that forms the primitive axial skeleton of the embryo and defines the body axis. It induces formation of the neural plate (and ultimately the neural tube) and persists in adults as the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs.
description_en: A rod-like structure of mesodermal origin that forms the primitive axial skeleton of the embryo and defines the body axis. It induces formation of the neural plate (and ultimately the neural tube) and persists in adults as the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The embryonic period (weeks 3-8) during which the major organ systems are established from the three germ layers. This is the period of greatest susceptibility to teratogens, as disruption at critical windows can cause major structural malformations.
description_en: The embryonic period (weeks 3-8) during which the major organ systems are established from the three germ layers. This is the period of greatest susceptibility to teratogens, as disruption at critical windows can cause major structural malformations.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: One of a series of mesodermal and neural crest-derived paired structures in the embryonic head and neck region (also called branchial arches), each containing a cartilaginous bar, a cranial nerve, and an aortic arch artery. They give rise to the bones, muscles, and vasculature of the face, jaw, and neck.
description_en: One of a series of mesodermal and neural crest-derived paired structures in the embryonic head and neck region (also called branchial arches), each containing a cartilaginous bar, a cranial nerve, and an aortic arch artery. They give rise to the bones, muscles, and vasculature of the face, jaw, and neck.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The discoid organ formed by the interlocking of the fetal chorion (trophoblast-derived) and the maternal decidua basalis (endometrium) that facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products between the fetal and maternal circulations without direct mixing of blood. It also produces hormones including hCG, progesterone, and estrogen.
description_en: The discoid organ formed by the interlocking of the fetal chorion (trophoblast-derived) and the maternal decidua basalis (endometrium) that facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products between the fetal and maternal circulations without direct mixing of blood. It also produces hormones including hCG, progesterone, and estrogen.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: Paired blocks of paraxial mesoderm that form in a cranial-to-caudal sequence during embryonic development. Each somite differentiates into a sclerotome (vertebrae and ribs), myotome (skeletal muscles of the trunk and limbs), and dermatome (dermis of the dorsal skin).
description_en: Paired blocks of paraxial mesoderm that form in a cranial-to-caudal sequence during embryonic development. Each somite differentiates into a sclerotome (vertebrae and ribs), myotome (skeletal muscles of the trunk and limbs), and dermatome (dermis of the dorsal skin).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif: The outer cell layer of the blastocyst that invades the uterine endometrium during implantation and differentiates into the cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast. It forms the fetal component of the placenta and produces human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), the hormone detected by pregnancy tests.
description_en: The outer cell layer of the blastocyst that invades the uterine endometrium during implantation and differentiates into the cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast. It forms the fetal component of the placenta and produces human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), the hormone detected by pregnancy tests.
